annotations.text:
Scores — three layout directions

Same content and tokens in all three (Plus Jakarta Sans, #f6f4f1 paper, #24382e accent, 20px cards). They differ in what the page puts first.

A — Triage queue

Closest to what is built. The ranked list is the page; analysis sits under it. Breakdown opens inline in the row.

Best for: scanning many roles quickly.
Tradeoff: "what should I do about it" is below the fold.

B — Verdict first

Leads with the pay gap drawn as one bar, then the single next action as a sentence, then one-skill-away roles. The list follows, compressed to a score and a title.

Best for: answering "where do I stand, what do I do" in one screen.
Tradeoff: browsing 57 roles means scrolling past the verdict every time.

C — Workbench

Filters and all four analyses live in a rail that stays put; the list and a docked detail panel fill the rest.

Best for: keeping context while working through the list — the detail swaps without the list moving.
Tradeoff: needs width, and the rail is dense. Would need a real plan for narrow screens.
